evals.prompt: Teach me what a message queue is and whether we need one.
evals.expected_output: Asks first whether the lesson is repo-anchored or standalone, then builds a docs/learn lesson with a runnable lab, four diagrams, provenance-tagged claims and, if repo-anchored, a fit map and audit task cards.
expectations: Asks the repo-anchored or standalone question before reading code or writing files
Tags every load-bearing claim measured, documented, rule of thumb or depends, and counts them in the masthead
Builds a zero-dependency lab that runs the counterfactual too
Plans the four diagrams: mechanism map, without/with, risks, neighbours
In repo-anchored mode, grades a fit map from a feature inventory read on the day and ends with A- audit cards

evals.prompt: Teach me our database platform and where we could use more of it. Base it on our current code.
evals.expected_output: A repo-anchored product lesson whose fit map starts from the project's needs and grades each capability honestly, including ruled-out rows that name the rule.
expectations: Inventories the project's features before listing the product's capabilities
Marks capabilities already in use with file, line and date
Grades a capability ruled out when it collides with a recorded decision, naming it
Never writes to the real instance from the lab
